requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is logged with the invoking user and a timestamp
requirements.summary: Sudoers drop-in /etc/sudoers.d/00-command-log sets Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log" with log_year enabled. Captured log lines show format 'Sep 29 08:05:10 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...' for multiple distinct sudo invocations (visudo, touch, chmod, chown, whoami, cat), demonstrating user and full timestamp are recorded per command.
File was created, permissioned 0600 root:root, and directly observed to contain the expected sudo log entries both before and after restart (16 then 26 lines).

requirements.requirement: Sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
requirements.summary: The '!syslog' Default disables sudo's syslog output. Step 7 of cmd-7cceca8f2fe54b44 shows /var/log/messages contains sudo entries only up through the install of the drop-in; none of the subsequent test commands (visudo, touch, chmod, chown, whoami, cat) appear in messages. Post-restart check (cmd-6328b0ecf4ef4370) confirms a new 'sudo id' command also does not leak into messages.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with recovered configuration, log data, and behavior
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (44767f03...) and healthy baseline (sudoers.d present, log file with 16 lines) were captured. A non-blocking sudo reboot was issued and acknowledged before disconnect. Three consecutive polls timed out (node down), then a poll succeeded with a different boot_id (7631fc37...), proving a real restart. Post-restart checks confirm the sudoers drop-in persisted, visudo parses OK, prior log lines were preserved (26 lines, i.e. baseline 16 plus new entries), and a new sudo command was correctly logged and still absent from /var/log/messages. Fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare vs after_executor) independently corroborate the boot_id change.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented sudo command logging on node1 via a sudoers.d drop-in using logfile and !syslog directives, directly verified that commands are logged with user/timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log and are absent from /var/log/messages, and completed the mandatory restart protocol with a clear pre/post boot-identity transition and confirmed post-restart recovery of configuration, log data, and logging behavior. The only minor blemish is a leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the backgrounded reboot command.
limitations: Log rotation/retention behavior for the new logfile was not verified, though not required by the task contract.
The small /tmp/reboot.log residue was not explicitly cleaned up, though it is harmless.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map clearly to task purposes: writing the sudoers.d drop-in and setting logfile permissions (required configuration), triggering test sudo commands (bounded verification of logging behavior), and issuing the mandated reboot (restart-evidence protocol). No destructive, unrelated, or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were observed; the three 'failed' commands (cmd-a0ea8271d5c44ff4, cmd-613065865a2d4a62, cmd-8d4b438e9aca4f09) are expected connection timeouts while the node was rebooting, not erroneous mutations. The only residue is a small /tmp/reboot.log file (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) created by the backgrounded reboot redirect; it is bounded, low-risk, and not cleaned up, so it is a minor unnecessary residue rather than a functional problem.
